validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #51 collects four non-blocking findings the review of PR #50 raised and approved despite. Three are in the two sqlite test files PR #50 touched; the fourth is a PR-metadata nit. I reproduced each against the default branch before planning, as the ticket asks.

(1) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:35 — the afterEach added by PR #50 calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which restores every spy the file holds, including the global.fetch spy that patchFetchForSqlJS installs in the top-level beforeAll (index.test.ts:17, via vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch') at mocks/util.ts:71). I verified this on this checkout by applying the proposed fix and then removing only the new beforeEach: with the fix in place the whole web config reports 16 passed; with only the beforeEach removed and the new regression test still present, it reports '× keeps the sql.js wasm fetch patched for every test, not just the first' with 'AssertionError: expected false to be true' and 'Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)' — the other nine sqlite tests and all six fs tests still pass. The suite stays green without the fix because init() runs once in the beforeAll and sql.js caches the compiled wasm, so this is latent rather than live — exactly as the review said. The fix the review proposed (re-arm the patch per test) works: patchFetchForSqlJS is a vi.spyOn(...).mockImplementation(...), so calling it again is idempotent.

The review also noted this leaves the file differing from its sibling fs/index.test.ts:20, which installs the same beforeAll fetch patch and was left alone. I checked why the sibling needs nothing: its afterEach (fs/index.test.ts:28-30) calls only sqlite._getModule().reset_filesystem() and never vi.restoreAllMocks(), so its fetch patch survives every test. The sibling is not a counterexample — it is the shape that has no bug. The divergence the review flagged is therefore correct after the fix, not a leftover.

(2) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.test.ts:143 — the comment block at lines 142-144 says `expect(handles).toHaveLength(0)` is 'above'. That assertion is at line 151, after teardown() at 148. grep confirms the only two occurrences of the string are the comment at 143 and the assertion at 151, in that order. One word is wrong.

(3) REPRODUCED, with the position corrected against the v1 plan this replaces. grep -nE '^  it\(|handles\.push|await openDatabase' on index.test.ts returns nine it() blocks opening at 41, 70, 110, 150, 198, 219, 260, 325, 381 and ten `await openDatabase()` calls at 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 341, 344, 382 — but `handles.push` only at 342 and 345. Both are inside the it() block that opens at line 325, titled 'should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process'. That is the eighth of the nine tests. The ninth and final test, opening at line 381, opens a database and never pushes it. So the comment at index.test.ts:28-31 is true of the mock half for every test and true of the handle half for that one named test only. (The v1 plan said 'the final test' in four places; its own cited line numbers said 325, and grep confirms 325. This plan refers to the test by title and line throughout, never by position in the file.)

(4) NOT A CODE CHANGE. PR #50's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix (.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md). PR #50 is MERGED, so there is no diff to carry this fix: the rule is enforced when a PR is opened, and .github/** is a forbidden path. The review itself notes every recent PR (37, 39, 40, 49) shares this shape, which makes it a pipeline-wide habit and not this ticket's code. Deferred to a human with the reason recorded.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #50 added a blanket vi.restoreAllMocks() to index.test.ts's afterEach and, separately, wrote two comments that claim more than the code does. The blanket restore reaches beyond the console spy AC-1 targeted, because vi.restoreAllMocks() is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped; the comments were written from the shape of the teardown rather than from which tests actually register a handle — the comment speaks of 'a handle' generically when exactly one test, the one opening at line 325, ever pushes one.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three small edits across the two files PR #50 touched, plus one regression test that fails without the fix.

The fetch patch moves from once-per-file to once-per-test. Hoist the existing baseURL template literal (currently computed inside the beforeAll at index.test.ts:16) to a module-scope const, keep patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) in the beforeAll where init({ baseURL }) needs it, and add a top-level beforeEach that calls patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) again. patchFetchForSqlJS is vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...), so re-spying a restored global is idempotent and the afterEach's blanket restore can no longer outrun it. This is the smaller of the two fixes the review offered — the other, narrowing the restore to the console spy alone, would mean hand-tracking the console spy and would break the deliberate mirroring of index.electron.test.ts's teardown().

A new test appended at the end of the describe asserts vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch) is true. Verified both directions on this checkout: with only the new beforeEach removed it fails with 'expected false to be true' while the other nine sqlite tests and all six fs tests pass. It must not be placed first — without the fix fetch is still patched during whichever test runs before the first afterEach, so a first-positioned assertion would pass for the wrong reason and be vacuous under -t filtering. A comment on the test must say so, matching the existing convention in index.electron.test.ts:129-137.

The two comment corrections are wording only. In index.test.ts:28-31 the comment is split so the mock half carries its true scope (every test) and the handle half names the one test that registers handles — the 'once per database handle' test opening at line 325 — instead of implying every openDatabase() handle is closed. In index.electron.test.ts:143 'above' becomes 'below'.

No production code changes. No new dependency. No behaviour change to anything outside the test files.

risks: The beforeEach re-arm is a new hook running before all ten tests in index.test.ts. patchFetchForSqlJS is a vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...), so the second and later calls reinstall the same mock on an already-restored global; if that ever stopped being true the suite would fail loudly on the new assertion rather than silently.

The re-arm only touches global.fetch within this one test file. vitest isolates files by default, so it cannot leak into fs/index.test.ts, which runs in the same vitest.web.config.ts project. fs/index.test.ts is deliberately left alone: its afterEach never calls vi.restoreAllMocks().

Touching only comments in index.electron.test.ts means that file's runtime behaviour is unchanged; the only risk is a bad find-and-replace landing the wrong 'above' or 'below'. AC-3 pins the direction.

The rewritten handle comment is a claim about which test registers handles, and a stale claim there is exactly the defect this ticket exists to fix. AC-4 pins it to a grep the QA agent can run, and the plan names the test by its title and line rather than by position, so the implementer cannot reintroduce the v1 plan's 'the final test' error while moving the comment.

In particular the [AI] PR-title rule lives in .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, which no ticket may change — that is why finding 4 is deferred.

Pushing handles.push(db) into the eight tests of index.test.ts that call openDatabase() without registering (lines 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 382). The review explicitly scopes this out and this ticket does the same: eight unclosed in-memory sql.js handles inside a test process that exits minutes later is not a leak worth a diff. This ticket corrects the comment instead — the reviewer's stated fix.
Making the handle leak visible at all, e.g. asserting no sql.js handle survives the suite. Nothing currently observes it and adding an observer would be a new mechanism for a non-defect.
Any change to production code. The fetch patch and the teardown are test-only; nothing under packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.ts is touched.

Moving the fetch patch to beforeEach only, dropping it from the beforeAll. init({ baseURL }) runs in the beforeAll and loads the wasm through the patched fetch, and beforeAll runs before the first beforeEach, so init would fetch unpatched.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: No decisions were recorded for this issue (plan/brief.md's 'Decided for this issue' section is empty). The only input beyond the ticket is the recorded rejection of the v1 plan, whose single objection was that four locations described the handle-registering test as 'the final test' / 'the last test' when grep places its it() block at line 325, the eighth of nine, with the block at line 381 never pushing a handle. Every one of those four locations — files[0].change, AC-4, qa_script step 6 and evidence[4] — now names the test by its title and line instead. The substance of v1 was re-verified on this checkout rather than inherited: baseline 15 passed, fix applied gives 16 passed, and removing only the new beforeEach gives '1 failed | 15 passed (16)' with 'expected false to be true'. The v1 claim that the new fetch test is 'the final test' was confirmed correct and is kept.
residual_risks: The new test asserts a vitest internal (vi.isMockFunction on a global) rather than application behaviour. It is a guard on the teardown contract this file relies on, and it is the only assertion in the file that would notice the fetch patch lapsing; if a future vitest changes isMockFunction semantics the test would need rewriting.
The rewritten comment's factual half can still drift if someone later adds handles.push to another test without updating it. AC-4 pins the current state rather than adding an observer.

AC-1 through AC-6 are all verify:'test'. There is no browser-observable surface to this ticket — it touches only two unit-test files — so no criterion is checkable against a live URL and none is written as if it were.
